summary: Ronald M. Davidson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 1985 and has held posts as Professor at California State University, Northridge and at Fairfield University.

Ronald Merry Macphail (1899–1974) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at The Glasgow Academy and the University of Glasgow (M.B., 1924), later holding posts with the Church of Scotland (1925) and the Bamdah Medical Mission (around 1925).

Ronald Morton Smith (1916–1999) worked in Indology. He studied at Bromsgrove School, St Andrews, Oxford, and Cambridge. He was a Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge (1948–1955), Assistant Professor at Toronto (1955–1982), and chairman at Harvard (1976–1978).

Ronald Neufeldt is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He spent his career at the University of Calgary (~1974–2007), serving as Associate Professor in the Religious Studies Department (~1980–1990) and becoming Professor Emeritus around 2007.

Ronald S. Green works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at UNC Charlotte, Virginia Tech, Oregon, and Wisconsin-Madison. His posts include Assistant Professor at Coastal Carolina University (attested 2013) and co-editor at ASIANetwork (2020–2025).

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1975–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng (1894–1983) was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and held a post at Yenching University (~1926–1941).

Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned her PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, later holding posts there and at the Center for Chinese Studies.

Ronit Ricci is an Indology, religious studies, and linguistics scholar. Educated at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, she has held posts at the Australian National University (2010) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem's Faculty of Humanities (2014).

Ronit Yoeli-Tlalim is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (1998–2004) and held posts at University College London (attested 2010) and Goldsmiths, University of London (Professor, 2023–2024).

Roper Lethbridge (1840–1919) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Exeter College (~1859–1863) and held posts with the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1878) and as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Roque Mesquita (1937–2016) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and under Gerhard Oberhammer at the University of Vienna, where he completed his doctorate and habilitation, serving on its faculty from 1972 to 2002.

Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp and Janet Gyatso, among others.
Rory Mackenzie is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He has held a post as a teacher at International Christian College.

Rosalind Lefeber is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Toronto under supervisors Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She also taught Sanskrit at the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

Rosalind O'Hanlon specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at SOAS (~1978–1983) and held posts at Clare College (~1988–2008), the University of Oxford as Professor in Indian History and Culture (~2008), and the British Academy (2020).

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1960–1969). He served on Komazawa's faculty from 1969 to 2012, becoming Professor in 1983, and was director at the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles under Ludo Rocher. She held posts at the NFSR (1961–1970), University of Pennsylvania from 1970, Meiji Gakuin University, and the Ludo and Rosane Rocher Foundation.

Rosemarie Fuchs is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg and completed her habilitation at Regensburg. She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994), Jena (1994–2013), and Humboldt University of Berlin (2013).
